label: Public tax, wage, rent and fee figures used by the SYNTHETIC rehearsal. Each names its source, date and URL as read. Figures for tax year 2026.

federal_2026.source: IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32 (tax year 2026 inflation adjustments, incl. Pub. L. 119-21 amendments), Oct 2025
federal_2026.salt_source: 26 USC 164(b)(6)-(7) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 sec. 70120, read at https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/164 (READ 2026-11-22)
federal_2026.qbi_source: 26 USC 199A(a), sunset in old (i) removed by Pub. L. 119-21 sec. 70105, read at https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/199A (READ 2026-11-22). Rental income gets no QBI deduction in this model (conservative: a rental counts only if it is a trade or business).

fees.source: 805 ILCS 180/50-10(b)(11) (LLC annual report); Illinois Attorney General AG990-IL Filing Instructions rev. 01/24
fees.corporate_trustee_note: Two trust companies' own published schedules, read 2026-11-25. Members Trust Company (NCSECU Trust Services Fee Schedule, April 2024, https://www.ncsecu.org/content/dam/ncsecu/pdfs/planning-insurance/estate-planning-and-trust-services/TrustServicesFeeSchedule.pdf): 'Minimum annual fees: ... $3,000 for Irrevocable Trusts', market value fee 'First $1 million 1.25%'. BOKF, NA (Advisor Trust Services fee schedule, revised 01.2027, https://edge.sitecorecloud.io/bokfna15473-bokf40a9-prode209-f913/media/Files/PDF/Advisor_Trust/ATS-Fee-Schedule.pdf): Directed Personal Trust 'First $1MM 0.50%', 'Minimum Annual Account fee $5,000'; 'Trust Management for Closely Held Assets, Tangible Assets & Collectibles' 'First $1MM 1.250%', 'Total balance less than $1MM 1.500%', 'Minimum Annual Account fee $4,000'. The engine takes the lowest minimum read for an irrevocable trust (3,000) and the 1.25 percent first-million rate that both schedules show for assets that are not marketable securities. A schedule is a list price for a managed trust, not a quote for a co-trustee who only decides distributions; hourly rates and out-of-pocket costs are extra (BOKF: '$200 per hour'). Citi and Schwab pages did not load (error page, HTTP refusal).

not_read: 26 USC 170(p) statute text: IRS IR-2026-135 says non-itemizers may deduct up to 1,000 (2,000 joint) of cash gifts from 2026, and gifts to supporting organizations and donor-advised funds do not qualify. Whether gifts to a private non-operating foundation qualify is NOT confirmed; the model gives them no deduction.

grantor_trust.source: 26 USC 674(a), (c), (d); 672(c); Treas. Reg. 1.671-4(b); read at law.cornell.edu 2026-11-22
grantor_trust.rule: A trust whose income can be sprinkled by the grantor (or a nonadverse party) is the grantor's for income tax (674(a)). The independent-trustee exception (674(c)) needs trustees none of whom is the grantor and no more than half related or subordinate (672(c): spouse, parents, issue, siblings, employees). A grantor trust with one owner may skip Form 1041 under the optional method (1.671-4(b)(2)(ii)(B)), unless it has a foreign situs or foreign assets (1.671-4(b)(6)).

cafeteria_125.quote: Except as provided in subsection (b), no amount shall be included in the gross income of a participant ... solely because, under the plan, the participant may choose among the benefits of the plan.
cafeteria_125.effect: A qualified benefit chosen under a cafeteria plan (e.g. health premiums) is left out of income-tax wages.

cafeteria_fica.quote: (G) under a cafeteria plan (within the meaning of section 125) if such payment would not be treated as wages ... it is reasonable to believe that (if section 125 applied for purposes of this section) ...
cafeteria_fica.effect: The same amount is left out of FICA wages (3121(a)(5)(G)).

elective_deferral_fica.quote: Nothing in any paragraph of subsection (a) (other than paragraph (1)) shall exclude from the term "wages"— (A) any employer contribution under a qualified cash or deferred arrangement (as defined in section 401(k)) to the extent not included in gross income by reason of section 402(e)(3) ...
elective_deferral_fica.effect: A 401(k) deferral is left out of income-tax wages (402(e)(3)) but stays in FICA wages (3121(v)(1)(A)).

payroll_pretax.not_read: 402(e)(3) itself and the 2026 402(g) deferral limit were not read; the synthetic deferral stays far below any limit.

excise_4940.rate_rule: 4940(a): 'a tax equal to 1.39 percent of the net investment income of such foundation for the taxable year.' The engine's 0.0139 matches.
excise_4940.base_rule: 4940(c)(2): gross investment income 'means the gross amount of income from interest, dividends, rents, payments with respect to securities loans (as defined in section 512(a)(5)), and royalties'. A contribution or the trust's 642(c) set-aside paid to the Foundation is not on that list, so it is not investment income; the engine's net_investment_income stays 0 until the Foundation holds assets that earn some. Not read: Treas. Reg. 53.4940-1 on whether a contribution can ever be gross investment income, and 4940(e) (the reduced-rate rule, which the 2019 flat rate replaced).

niit.threshold_note: 1411(b)(3): $200,000 'in any other case' (joint 250,000 under (b)(1)). Statutory, not inflation-indexed.
niit.trust_rule: 1411(a)(2): 'a tax of 3.8 percent of the lesser of (A) the undistributed net investment income for such taxable year, or (B) the excess (if any) of (i) the adjusted gross income (as defined in section 67(e)) for such taxable year, over (ii) the dollar amount at which the highest tax bracket in section 1(e) begins for such taxable year.' The engine uses the last trust_brackets entry.
niit.individual_rule: 1411(a)(1): '3.8 percent of the lesser of (A) net investment income for such taxable year, or (B) the excess (if any) of (i) the modified adjusted gross income for such taxable year, over (ii) the threshold amount.'
niit.nii_definition: 1411(c)(1)(A): gross income from interest, dividends, annuities, royalties and rents not derived in the ordinary course of a trade or business not described in (c)(2); (c)(2): a passive activity under 469, or trading in financial instruments or commodities. (c)(6): items taken into account in self-employment income are excluded.
niit.assumption: ASSUMPTION: the founder's rentals and the bought business (hired manager, no material participation) are passive, so their net income is net investment income; consulting is self-employment income and is not. A real-estate-professional or material-participation election would remove it; a counsel/CPA question. Trust AGI is approximated by retained income (distribution deduction taken first); deductions allocable to NII are netted in asset_net.

irc_4942.note: Page not read in this run (no web read); cited from the backlog item. The engine's fixed 5 percent program figure and the fixed_assets program_source use this rate.

irc_642_c_1.note: Page not read in this run. ASSUMPTION (counsel-queue.md Q9): the trust's payment to the Foundation is a charitable set-aside paid from gross income; it makes the trust a 4947(a)(2) split-interest trust.

kiddie_tax.source: 26 USC 1(g), 152(c)(3), IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32 sec. 3.02 and 3.14(2), IRS Instructions for Form 8615 (2025); read 2026-11-25
kiddie_tax.who_it_covers: 1(g)(2)(A): '(i) has not attained age 18 before the close of the taxable year' (the page's text for (ii): a child who has reached 18, meets the 152(c)(3) age requirements applied without regard to its subparagraph (B), and whose earned income does not exceed one-half of the individual's support); 1(g)(2)(B): a parent is alive at year end. 152(c)(3)(A): the individual '(i) has not attained the age of 19 as of the close of the calendar year' or '(ii) is a student who has not attained the age of 24 as of the close of such calendar year'. The Form 8615 instructions state it in plain words: under 18 at year end; 18 and 'didn't have earned income that was more than half of the child's support'; or 'a full-time student at least age 19 and under age 24' with the same support test.
kiddie_tax.how_taxed: 1(g)(1): the tax is 'the greater of' (A) 'the tax imposed by this section without regard to this subsection' or (B) the tax on the child's taxable income reduced by the net unearned income, plus the child's share of the 'allocable parental tax'. 1(g)(3): the allocable parental tax is 'the tax which would be imposed by this section on the parent's taxable income if such income included' the net unearned income of the children, less 'the tax imposed by this section on the parent without regard to this subsection.' 1(g)(4)(A): net unearned income is the excess of (i) 'the portion of the adjusted gross income for the taxable year which is not attributable to earned income' over (ii) the sum of (I) the 63(c)(5)(A) amount plus (II) the greater of that amount or directly connected itemized deductions. 1(g)(4)(B): 'shall not exceed the individual's taxable income'.
kiddie_tax.dollar_amounts_2026: Rev. Proc. 2025-32 sec. 3.02: 'the amount in 1(g)(4)(A)(ii)(I) ... is $1,350. This $1,350 amount is the same as the amount provided in 63(c)(5)(A)'. Sec. 3.14(2), dependent standard deduction: 'cannot exceed the greater of (1) $1,350, or (2) the sum of $450 and the individual's earned income.' So the first 1,350 of unearned income is covered by the dependent standard deduction, the next 1,350 is taxed at the child's rate, and the rest (net unearned income) at the parent's rate; the engine's `step` is 1,350.
kiddie_tax.niit_for_a_child: Instructions for Form 8615 (2025): 'A child whose tax is figured on Form 8615 may be subject to the NIIT. NIIT is a 3.8% tax on the lesser of net investment income or the excess of the child's modified adjusted gross income (MAGI) over the threshold amount. Use Form 8960 ... to figure this tax.' So the child's own MAGI is tested against the 200,000 threshold (1411(b)(3)), not the parent's. The 2025 instructions are the latest version read; the statute 1411 has no kiddie-tax rule. Exception read: a parent who elects Form 8814 puts the child's income on the parent's own Form 8960 (Instructions for Form 8960, line 7).
kiddie_tax.engine: rehearsal_run.py kiddie_split and minor_tax. Not modeled: the 1(g)(7) parental election, a minor's earned income, a minor's QBI, the Illinois exemption.
kiddie_tax.assumption: ASSUMPTION: a minor beneficiary has no other income, is under 18, and a parent is living; the household's minors are scenario facts only (`minor_beneficiaries`), never a description of anyone.

mgmt_c_corp.source: 26 USC 11(b), read at https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/11 (READ 2026-11-25): 'The amount of the tax imposed by subsection (a) shall be 21 percent of taxable income.' Qualified dividend rates: IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32 section 3.03 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf, READ 2026-11-25): for 2026, 'All Other Individuals' maximum zero rate amount $49,450, maximum 15 percent rate amount $545,500 (1(h), 1(j)(5)); the rate is 20 percent above.
mgmt_c_corp.dividend_rule: 1(h)(11) (taxed at the 1(h) rates, stacked on top of ordinary taxable income) and 1411(c)(1)(A)(i) (dividends are net investment income); both as cited in counsel-queue.md Q34, not re-read in this run.
mgmt_c_corp.illinois: NOT MODELED. Illinois corporate rates (35 ILCS 5/201) are pending, needs Dalaun (packet/NEEDS-DALAUN.md, Q34 claim 11); the c_corp option leaves Illinois corporate tax out, which makes the option look cheaper than it is. Illinois individual tax on the salary and the dividend is modeled (4.95 percent).
mgmt_c_corp.fringe_flags: From counsel-queue.md Q34 (read 2026-11-25): 106 and insured 105(b) allowed for an employee of a C corporation; 127 and 129 off because one owner-employee fails 127(b)(3) and 129(d)(4); 105(h), 79(d) and 132(j)(1) are check lines for counsel. The flags are inputs and carry no dollar amount in the engine (no cost source); no fringe lowers the founder's tax here.
mgmt_c_corp.assumption: ASSUMPTION: the corporation pays out all its after-tax profit as a qualified dividend in the year (no retained earnings, so no 531 accumulated-earnings issue and no 543(a)(7) personal holding company issue modeled); the salary is a stated input (mgmt_founder_salary) that must be reasonable for the services (162(a)(1)); the employer share of FICA on the salary is deducted by the corporation.
